1.explanation:
• ContentSwitcher/ContentSwitcher.mdx: the primary usage, markup, and style tokens for the ContentSwitcher component—needed to see its default fill, outline, and theming values.  
• Tabs/Tabs.mdx: underlying tab container behaviors and styling that ContentSwitcher builds upon—useful for understanding state handling and CSS selectors.  
• TabContent/TabContent.mdx: the child panel implementation showing how active/inactive states are managed—important for reproducing the interactive state changes and inspecting CSS applied to unselected tabs and divider elements.
1.bug_scenario:
The issue occurs in the Carbon ContentSwitcher component when two or more tabs are rendered side by side and the unselected tabs use a light-grey fill or 1px light-grey outline against a white background. In the provided screenshots:  

• The first screenshot (accessibility checker) shows that the unselected tab’s light-grey outline/fill fails the WCAG 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast ratio (measured ~1.1:1, must be ≥3:1).  
• The second screenshot shows multiple style variations (default, no-fill, outline only, stripped, higher‐contrast divider, etc.) for two- and three-tab switchers, demonstrating how removing or bumping up contrast on the unselected tab highlights or hides the component boundary.  
• The third annotated zoom highlights (1) the selected tab (black) and (2) the unselected tab’s low-contrast styling that users can overlook.  

Because the outline/fill of the unselected tab and the divider between tabs fail the required contrast threshold, users can’t reliably perceive the ContentSwitcher component as a unified control, especially in low-resolution or noisy contexts.
